events.title: Leon Trotsky Attacked in Mexico
events.description: Soviet agent Ramón Mercader struck Leon Trotsky in the head with an ice axe at his home in Coyoacán, Mexico City. Trotsky died of his wounds the following day.
events.significance: The attack ended the life of a leading Bolshevik revolutionary and Stalin's most prominent exiled opponent, showing the reach of Soviet state violence beyond its borders.

events.title: Voyager 2 Launched
events.description: NASA launched the Voyager 2 spacecraft from Cape Canaveral, Florida, about two weeks before its twin, Voyager 1. It went on to fly by Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
events.significance: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune, and it later entered interstellar space in 2018, returning vast amounts of data about the outer solar system.

events.title: Soviet-Led Invasion of Czechoslovakia
events.description: Warsaw Pact forces, led by the Soviet Union, invaded Czechoslovakia on the night of August 20-21 to halt Alexander Dubcek's liberalizing reforms known as the Prague Spring.
events.significance: The invasion crushed the reform movement, reinforced the Brezhnev Doctrine of limited sovereignty in the Eastern Bloc, and drew worldwide condemnation.

events.title: First Commercial Radio News Broadcast
events.description: Detroit station 8MK (later WWJ) began regular programming, including news broadcasts, and is often cited as the first commercial radio news station in the United States.
events.significance: It marked an early step in the rise of broadcast journalism and commercial radio as a mass medium.

events.title: Birth of Benjamin Harrison
events.description: Benjamin Harrison, who would become the 23rd President of the United States, was born in North Bend, Ohio. He was the grandson of President William Henry Harrison.
events.significance: Harrison's presidency from 1889 to 1893 saw the passage of the Sherman Antitrust Act and the admission of several western states to the Union.
